definitions.explanation: Selling goods by traveling from place to place rather than operating from a fixed store. The person who does this is called a {行商人|ぎょうしょうにん}.

examples.japanese: {行商|ぎょうしょう}で{生計|せいけい}を{立|た}てる。
examples.english: To make a living by peddling.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}は{魚|さかな}の{行商|ぎょうしょう}が{町|まち}を{回|まわ}っていた。
examples.english: In the old days, fish peddlers would go around town.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{若|わか}い{頃|ころ}、リヤカーを{引|ひ}いて{野菜|やさい}の{行商|ぎょうしょう}をしていたそうだ。
examples.english: I heard my grandfather used to peddle vegetables pulling a cart when he was young.

notes:
Composed of {行|ぎょう} (travel/go) + {商|しょう} (commerce/trade). Refers to the practice of selling goods by going from place to place, rather than from a fixed shop.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {行商|ぎょうしょう}する: to peddle, to sell door-to-door
- {行商|ぎょうしょう}{人|にん}: peddler, traveling salesperson
- {行商|ぎょうしょう}に{出|で}る: to go out peddling

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {露店|ろてん}: street stall — a temporary booth set up in one place
- {物売|ものう}り: vendor, seller — more general term

CULTURAL NOTE:
Traditional {行商|ぎょうしょう} was common in Japan before the spread of supermarkets. Fish, tofu, and vegetable peddlers would walk through neighborhoods. While rare today, some traveling vendors still operate in rural areas.
